questions.q: Chidi and other traders in Kano want to form a business organisation that can sue and be sued in its own name, has limited liability for its members and is managed by a board of directors. Which business unit best fits this description?
questions.explanation: A limited liability company is incorporated, so it has a separate legal personality, can sue and be sued, and its members' liability is limited. A sole proprietorship and an ordinary partnership are not separate legal entities with limited liability in this way, while a trade association is not primarily a profit-making business unit.

questions.q: A supermarket owned by Ada in Lagos insures its cashier against loss of up to ₦500,000 arising from dishonesty and embezzlement. Which class of insurance covers this risk?
questions.explanation: Fidelity guarantee insurance protects an employer against financial loss caused by the dishonesty of employees entrusted with money or property. Marine insurance covers goods and vessels in transit, while employer's liability insurance deals with injury or illness suffered by employees in the course of work.

questions.q: A retail store in Abuja sells foodstuffs, toiletries and household items on a self-service basis, and customers pay at checkout counters. This type of retailer is best described as a...
questions.explanation: A supermarket is a large self-service retail outlet dealing mainly in food and household goods, with payment made at checkout points. A department store is organised into separate departments selling different lines, while a specialist shop concentrates on one category of goods.

questions.q: Chika, a wholesaler in Onitsha, supplies goods to a retailer now and allows payment after the retailer has sold them. This service is known as...
questions.explanation: Granting credit is the wholesaler's service of allowing the retailer time to pay for goods after delivery. Breaking bulk refers to dividing large quantities into smaller lots, while warehousing and transportation are separate storage and movement services.

questions.q: A supplier in Enugu sends a buyer in Awka a document listing all transactions between them during the month and showing the balance due. This document is a...
questions.explanation: A statement of account summarises transactions over a period and shows the amount owed by or due to the buyer. A pro forma invoice is sent before supply to show the estimated cost, while a credit note records a reduction in the amount payable.

questions.q: A trader in Lagos sends goods by road to a customer in Ibadan. The document issued by the transport company showing details of the goods and the conditions of carriage is a...
questions.explanation: A waybill is used for goods carried by road or rail and gives details of the consignment and the terms of carriage. A bill of lading is specifically used for sea carriage, while an invoice shows the amount payable for goods and a credit note records a reduction.

questions.q: A buyer in Ilorin wants a supplier in Aba to send a stated quantity and description of goods. Which document should the buyer use to place the request?
questions.explanation: A purchase order is sent by a buyer to a seller to request specified goods and state the quantity, description and delivery requirements. A delivery note accompanies goods already being sent, a statement of account summarises transactions, and a debit note records an additional amount owed.

questions.q: A manager in Ikeja sends an instruction to a branch supervisor in Surulere by telephone. The main advantage of this channel over a written memorandum is that it...
options: is always cheaper for long messages
questions.explanation: A telephone conversation enables the manager and supervisor to ask questions and clear up misunderstandings at once. A written memorandum is better for providing a permanent record, but it is not necessarily cheaper for long messages and does not guarantee confidentiality.

questions.q: Which of the following is classified as a primary occupation?
questions.explanation: Quarrying is a primary occupation because it involves extracting raw materials directly from nature. Baking of bread and road construction are secondary activities, while banking is a tertiary service occupation.

questions.q: A furniture-maker uses timber, nails and varnish costing ₦180,000 to produce chairs that he sells for ₦250,000. What is the value added by the furniture-maker?
questions.explanation: Value added is the selling value of output minus the cost of intermediate goods used. Here, ₦250,000 − ₦180,000 = ₦70,000. The figure ₦250,000 is total sales, while ₦180,000 is the cost of intermediate materials, not value added.

questions.q: Which of the following best illustrates capital-intensive production?
options: Using automated bottling machines in a water factory
Employing many labourers to load trucks manually
Selling goods in a retail shop
questions.explanation: Capital-intensive production uses a large amount of machinery and equipment relative to labour, as in an automated bottling plant. Manual loading and hoe-and-cutlass farming rely more heavily on labour, while retail selling is a service activity.

questions.q: A shareholder who is unable to attend a company's annual general meeting authorizes another person to attend and vote on his behalf. The person so authorized is known as a...
questions.explanation: A proxy is the person appointed by a shareholder to attend a company meeting and vote in place of the shareholder. A stockbroker trades securities, a debenture holder is a creditor of the company, and a registrar keeps share records.

questions.q: An investor who buys shares mainly in anticipation that their market prices will rise so that he can sell them later at a profit is known as a...
questions.explanation: A bull expects share prices to rise and therefore buys now hoping to sell at a profit later. A bear expects prices to fall, while a stockbroker buys and sells securities on behalf of clients rather than necessarily speculating on price movements.

questions.q: An advertisement whose main purpose is to give customers factual details about a newly introduced product is best described as...
questions.explanation: Informative advertising introduces a product and supplies factual details such as its features, uses or price. Reminder advertising keeps an established brand in customers' minds, while institutional advertising promotes the image of an organization rather than a particular product.

questions.q: A small firm sells its products directly to consumers through its own online store without using wholesalers or retailers. This is an example of...
questions.explanation: Direct distribution occurs when a producer sells straight to final consumers without intermediaries. Indirect distribution uses middlemen, while exclusive and intensive distribution describe how widely a product is made available rather than whether intermediaries are used.

questions.q: A trader in Kano displays an electric iron whose controls are labelled only in a foreign language and supplies no instruction leaflet. A buyer who cannot understand how to operate the iron is most directly denied the consumer right to
questions.explanation: The right to information requires a seller to provide adequate details and instructions about the use of a product. The missing leaflet and foreign-language controls directly prevent the buyer from being properly informed, while redress becomes relevant only after loss or injury.

questions.q: A pharmaceutical company in Lagos withdraws a batch of cough syrup from shops after tests show that it is contaminated. The action is primarily intended to protect consumers' right to
questions.explanation: The right to safety protects consumers from goods that may cause harm, and withdrawing contaminated syrup prevents injury before it occurs. Redress is compensation after harm has been suffered, not the main reason for withdrawing the batch.

questions.q: Binta borrows ₦480,000 from a microfinance bank at 10% simple interest per annum for 9 months. How much interest will she pay at the end of the period?
questions.explanation: Simple interest is ₦480,000 × 10/100 × 9/12 = ₦36,000. Using the full year gives ₦48,000, but the amount is borrowed for only nine months.

questions.q: A Nigerian shipping company earns ₦12 million by transporting imported goods from Apapa port to importers in Lagos. In Nigeria's balance of payments, this earning is classified under
questions.explanation: Shipping is a service, so the earnings from it form part of invisible trade. Visible trade involves tangible goods, while capital account and unilateral transfers deal with assets and gifts respectively.

questions.q: An online store in Abuja installs a digital certificate on its checkout page. The main purpose of the certificate is to
options: guarantee timely delivery of all orders
increase the website's ranking on search engines
secure communication and prove the website's identity
encrypt all data stored permanently in the seller's database
questions.explanation: A digital certificate supports secure web connections by helping to authenticate the website and enabling encrypted communication with customers. It does not guarantee delivery performance or secure all data stored permanently on the seller's database.

questions.q: The main aim of consumer education is to enable consumers to
options: obtain automatic replacement of every product after purchase
make informed buying decisions and exercise their rights responsibly
force traders to sell goods at government-controlled prices
prevent all imported goods from entering the local market
questions.explanation: Consumer education gives buyers knowledge and skills for making informed choices and claiming their rights when necessary. It does not give automatic replacement for every product or control prices and imports.

questions.q: A company in Lagos that supplies office furniture sells directly to another company in Abuja through its website. The transaction is best described as
questions.explanation: Both the seller and the buyer are businesses, so the transaction is business-to-business e-commerce. A sale to an individual final user would be business-to-consumer e-commerce.

questions.q: To protect local rice farmers, the Nigerian government limits the quantity of imported rice that may enter the country each year. This trade restriction is called
questions.explanation: An import quota places a physical limit on the quantity of a good that may be imported within a period. A tariff is a tax on imports, an export subsidy supports exporters, and an embargo is a general ban on trade.

questions.q: A group of market traders in Onitsha formed an association to save money regularly and grant loans to members at low interest. This association is best described as a...
questions.explanation: The association described mainly mobilises members' regular savings and lends to members at low interest, which is the purpose of a thrift and credit cooperative society. A consumer cooperative mainly buys goods for members, while a producer cooperative processes or markets members' produce. A multipurpose cooperative combines several functions rather than being formed solely for savings and credit.

questions.q: Which business organisation can raise long-term loan capital from the public by issuing debentures?
questions.explanation: A public limited liability company may invite the public to subscribe for shares and debentures, so it can raise long-term loan capital through debentures. A private limited company cannot invite the public to subscribe for its securities, while a partnership and a sole proprietorship cannot issue debentures to the public. The ability to borrow from the public in this way is therefore a feature of the public limited company.

questions.q: Which class of insurance is not based on the principle of indemnity?
questions.explanation: Life assurance pays a fixed sum assured on death or survival, rather than compensating the insured for the exact financial loss suffered, so the principle of indemnity does not apply to it. Fire, marine and motor insurances are generally contracts of indemnity that restore the insured to the financial position before the loss. This is why the class not based on indemnity is life assurance.

questions.q: A factory owner in Ikeja wants protection against claims from workers injured while operating machines. Which insurance cover is most appropriate?
questions.explanation: Employers' liability insurance protects an employer against legal claims by workers who are injured or become ill in the course of employment. Public liability insurance covers claims from visitors or outsiders, while fidelity guarantee insurance covers loss from dishonest employees. Marine insurance relates to sea transport risks and does not directly cover workplace injuries.

questions.q: When an insurance company transfers part of a very large risk it has accepted to another insurance company, the arrangement is called...
questions.explanation: Reinsurance occurs when an insurer transfers part of a risk it has accepted to another insurer in order to reduce its own exposure. Double insurance arises when the same insured takes out more than one policy on the same risk, while subrogation and contribution are principles applied after a loss. The transfer of risk between insurers is therefore reinsurance.

questions.q: A wholesaler who sells goods for cash only to retailers and requires them to arrange their own transport is best described as a...
questions.explanation: A cash-and-carry wholesaler sells goods strictly for cash and expects the retailer to arrange transport, so no credit or delivery service is provided. General-line and specialist wholesalers are classified mainly by the range of goods they handle. A manufacturer's agent negotiates sales but does not take title to the goods.

questions.q: A retail organisation with several branches in different towns, owned and controlled by one company and selling similar lines of goods, is called a...
questions.explanation: A multiple shop has several branches under one ownership and common management, usually selling similar lines of goods. A department store has many departments under one roof, while a supermarket is a large self-service retail outlet. A consumer cooperative store is owned and controlled by its members.

questions.q: A company in Ibadan must send original land title documents to a client in Abuja and obtain proof that they were received. Which service is most suitable?
questions.explanation: A courier service physically delivers the original documents and can provide a signed record of receipt. Ordinary letter post does not give reliable proof of delivery, while telephone calls and electronic mail cannot deliver the original title documents.

questions.q: A haulage company charges ₦4,200 per tonne for the first 20 tonnes and ₦3,800 per tonne for every additional tonne. What is the total charge for transporting 60 tonnes of cement from Ogun State to Adamawa State?
questions.explanation: The first 20 tonnes cost 20 × ₦4,200 = ₦84,000. The remaining 40 tonnes cost 40 × ₦3,800 = ₦152,000. The total charge is ₦84,000 + ₦152,000 = ₦236,000.

questions.q: A textile company in Kaduna buys raw cotton worth ₦450,000 and uses it to produce cloth which it sells for ₦1,200,000. What is the value added by the company?
questions.explanation: Value added is the difference between the value of output and the cost of intermediate goods purchased. It is ₦1,200,000 − ₦450,000 = ₦750,000. The raw cotton cost is not added again because it is already included in the selling value of the cloth.

questions.q: A worker in a shoe factory in Aba takes leather and other materials and converts them into finished shoes. This worker is mainly engaged in which type of production?
questions.explanation: Secondary production involves processing raw materials into finished or semi-finished goods, as in manufacturing shoes. Primary or extractive production obtains raw materials directly from nature, while tertiary production provides services.

questions.q: When a public company offers its existing shareholders the first chance to buy new shares, usually at a price below the market price, before they are offered to outsiders, this is called:
questions.explanation: A rights issue gives existing shareholders the right to buy additional new shares, often at a discount, in proportion to their existing holdings. A bonus issue gives free shares, a debenture issue involves debt, and an initial public offering is the first sale of shares to the general public.

questions.q: An investor buys 1,000 shares of a bank at ₦12.50 per share through a stockbroker on the Nigerian Exchange. If the brokerage commission is 2% of the cost of the shares, what is the total amount paid by the investor?
questions.explanation: The cost of the shares is 1,000 × ₦12.50 = ₦12,500. The brokerage commission is 2% of ₦12,500 = ₦250. The total amount paid is ₦12,500 + ₦250 = ₦12,750.

questions.q: A soft-drink company in Lagos runs adverts during festive periods to remind consumers about its existing brand without giving new information. This type of advertising is best described as:
questions.explanation: Reminder advertising keeps an already established brand in consumers’ minds, especially during periods when demand may rise. Informative advertising provides new facts, persuasive advertising tries to convince consumers to choose a brand, and primary demand advertising promotes a whole product category rather than one brand.

questions.q: A detergent company in Ibadan gives small free packets of its new washing powder to households in a new market to encourage them to try the product. This promotional technique is called:
questions.explanation: Sampling involves giving free samples of a product so that consumers can try it and possibly become regular buyers. Publicity is unpaid attention from the media, personal selling involves direct oral persuasion, and advertising is paid non-personal promotion.

questions.q: A grain seller in Kano uses a scale adjusted so that each 10 kg bag of rice weighs only 9 kg on the scale. Which consumer protection offence is the seller committing?
options: Using false or inaccurate weighing equipment
Refusing to give a receipt for cash payment
questions.explanation: The seller is deceiving buyers about quantity by tampering with a measuring instrument, which is a prohibited unfair trade practice. Failure to display price tags or issue receipts may breach other rules, but the specific offence here is inaccurate weighing.

questions.q: The Standards Organisation of Nigeria mark on a carton of electrical cables mainly assures a buyer that the cables
options: conform to specified quality and safety standards
are sold at the approved government price
carry a longer warranty than other brands
questions.explanation: The Standards Organisation of Nigeria mark indicates that a product has met the relevant quality and safety standards. It does not by itself prove where the product was manufactured, guarantee a particular warranty period, or fix the selling price.
